newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures end higher, most below peaks.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures end higher, most below peaks.

text.p: U.S. debt futures ended moderately higher, but most closed below the day's peaks as the market braced for Friday's July U.S. employment figures.
They looked for nonfarm payrolls growth of 193,000 jobs, a drop in the jobless rate to 4.9 percent and a 0.2 percent rise in hourly earnings.

Some said the market's resilience Thursday underscored the bullish bias and said any further rise off from the jobs figures likely would feed on itself, as shorts bail out and more mortgage servicers capitulate and buy T-bond futures or options to hedge against rising prepayment risk as rates drop.

"This market still had a bid at the close," said one floor broker, noting that the 10-year cash note clung to the key 6.0 percent yield level and the current 30-year yield hit 6.30 percent. "We also met some important technical targets."

September T-bond futures had backed off from 117-00 as longs showed disappointment they were unable to clear there and hit big buystops. Some saw size bank selling on the brief subsequent return to the minus side. One broker also noted talk of big cash mortgage paper sales on move back down.
But futures shook off pressure and drew paper buying on the dips, in character with the pattern of the recent rally.
In the Eurodollar pit, a floor broker said that one French bank affiliate by midday had bought between 15,000 and 19,000 December futures "all the way up."
Traders decided Thursday's data did little to disturb the idyllic view of the economy that focuses on low inflation and moderate growth.

Advance second-quarter U.S. gross domestic product rose 2.2 percent from a downwardly revised 4.9 percent growth in the first quarter and compared with forecasts for 1.9 percent Q2 increase. The two price indexes each rose at a 1.4 percent rate, the smallest quarterly gains in more than 30 years.

Futures also firmed when the American Production and Inventory Control Society business outlook index rose to 53.0 in July versus forecasts for 53.3. But they glossed over weekly U.S. jobless that fell to 277,000 versus forecasts for 306,000, linking the drop largely to seasonal factors.
The July Chicago purchaser's index fell to 60.6 versus forecasts for 59.8. Prices paid rose, but employment fell.

Sept T-bonds rose 12/32 to 116-24/32, 10-year notes gained 8/32 to 111-00, munis firmed 3/32 to 122-05/32, Dec T-bills rose 0.030 to 94.905 and Eurodollars gained 0.030 to 94.215. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750))
